study: PromptPrism Multi-Model Hugging Face Factorial Benchmark Study

variance_decomposition_and_truncation_ru.item_contrast_definition: c_{S, i} = (2 / K) * sum_c X_{c, S} * Y_{c, i}
variance_decomposition_and_truncation_ru.analytical_sampling_variance: Var_hat(tau_hat_S) = s^2(c_{S, .}) / N_eval (ddof=1 across evaluated items)
variance_decomposition_and_truncation_ru.observed_rms: RMS_obs = sqrt((1 / |O|) * sum_{S in O} tau_hat_S^2)
variance_decomposition_and_truncation_ru.noise_floor_rms: RMS_noise = sqrt((1 / |O|) * sum_{S in O} Var_hat(tau_hat_S))
variance_decomposition_and_truncation_ru.rationale: Per-cube truncation records the exact fraction of individual cubes whose observed contrast power falls at or below the item-sampling variance floor (`frac_cubes_truncated_zero`), while cohort-level aggregation averages the unbiased variance component `sigma2_hat_signal_unclipped` across cubes prior to square-root truncation so multi-cube cohorts remain unbiased under pure noise even for |O|=1.

effect_hierarchy_audit.question: Is the apparent lack of effect hierarchy (2FI ~ 3FI ~ 4FI observed RMS on single-template MMLU) an item-sampling noise-floor artifact or genuine higher-order contrast structure?
effect_hierarchy_audit.concise_conclusion: Both mechanisms act simultaneously, and cross-cohort/stratum comparisons separate them cleanly: (1) On per-task MMLU (`legacy_first`), the observed Split-0 plateau (2FI=0.00724, 3FI=0.00725, 4FI=0.00738) is 76.8%-84.1% item-sampling variance (mean cube noise RMS 0.00677-0.00688, split-half r=0.14-0.17, 42.8%-47.6% of cubes truncated at zero); noise subtraction cuts Orders 2-4 RMS by more than half (0.00320 / 0.00336 / 0.00409 cohort RMS_corr) and separates 1FI (0.00732) >> {2FI, 3FI, 4FI} >> 5FI (0.00109). (2) However, among Orders 2-4, approximate parity (2FI ~ 3FI ~ 4FI) SURVIVES noise correction and persists with high 20-split item repeatability (r=0.89-0.90) on 14,042-item Pooled MMLU (0.00238 / 0.00239 / 0.00274) and single-template SLAB (0.0650 / 0.0688 / 0.0824). (3) Stratum averaging (`cell_mean_unique`) proves why: on SLAB, averaging out single-template wording idiosyncrasies restores strict monotonic hierarchy (1FI > 2FI > 3FI > 4FI: 0.0773 > 0.0390 > 0.0327 > 0.0284 cohort RMS_corr), whereas on MMLU `cell_mean_unique` reduces Pooled 3FI/4FI by 27.0%/31.2% (to 0.00174 / 0.00188 vs 2FI 0.00200) while retaining genuine multi-bit contrasts induced by binary partitioning of the 4-level `op` and 11-level `sep` categorical axes.
